editorial.headline: Air-Transport Equipment Wholesale: Open Nationally, Closed to PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Wholesale air-transport equipment, parts and accessories are nationally open to full foreign ownership, but Bali’s permanent risk-class moratorium blocks PMA registration.
editorial.body:
**KBLI 46594** covers wholesale trade in a range of air-transport equipment and, alongside the equipment itself, wholesale trade in its parts and accessories. Both elements are part of the stated scope: the equipment, and the components and fittings associated with it. It is a classification for the wholesale side of that commercial activity. The inclusion of parts and accessories is explicit rather than incidental. The scope therefore places equipment and its associated components in the same wholesale undertaking. For a founder reading the boundary, the essential point is simple: this is trade in air-transport equipment and the parts and accessories that belong to that trade, at wholesale level.

It can be registered at every scale named in the record—Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. That availability matters because it does not confine the activity to a single band of business scale. Nationally, its PMA status is TERBUKA and foreign ownership may reach 100%. The national reference listed for that position is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Taken on its national terms, therefore, the activity is fully open to foreign ownership, not merely open with a partial foreign stake.

Bali produces a different answer. A foreign investor cannot register this activity as PMA in Bali today. The Bali classification is Blocked (risk class): at the Besar scale, OSS risk is Low or Medium-Low across every scope. Bali’s permanent, island-wide moratorium blocks PMA registration for all KBLI activities in the Low and Medium-Low risk bands. The stated Bali source is Gubernur letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP. The obstruction is not a reduction of the national foreign-ownership ceiling; it is a block on PMA registration in Bali for an activity in those risk classes.

The distinction has to be held plainly rather than smoothed over. The national record says 100% foreign ownership is permitted, and the activity is available from Mikro to Besar. The Bali record says the PMA route is blocked under the provincial risk-class moratorium. For a business considering this precise activity, those statements are both true at once: national foreign ownership is fully open, while Bali does not presently admit a PMA registration for it.
editorial.pullQuote: A foreign investor cannot register this activity as PMA in Bali today.
